result.summary:
Fetched origin, checked out feature/WF03-ISS0692-20260917 (already up to date with its own remote). origin/main had moved 5 commits ahead (WF03-ISS0699 work, unrelated) since this branch was cut -- `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` confirmed main was NOT an ancestor. Ran `git merge origin/main`, which produced a clean merge commit with zero conflicts (only handoffs/orchestrator.log and handoffs/registry.json changed, both additive) -- consistent with the dispatch's prediction that this branch's four affected files don't overlap concurrent work. Pushed.

Opened PR #1472 (docs(ISS-0692): REQ-362 visual-baseline design gains binding synthetic-data-only policy), body summarizing the fix per ISS-0692's resolution_note and the gate chain, ending with the standard attribution footer.

Polled `gh pr checks 1472` synchronously in a bounded loop (30s interval). First run: Frontend gate and 'Detect changed paths' passed; 'Backend gate (mix letflow.check)' FAILED in 51s. Diagnosed for real rather than assuming the known ISS-0418 wasm_hang flake (that flake's signature -- main suite green, only an isolated wasm_hang subprocess stage red -- did not match; this failure was a hard, non-test step). Pulled the job's full log (`gh run view --job --log`) and found the actual cause: `letflow.lint_handoffs: FAIL -- 2 new (un-grandfathered) violation(s)`, both inside this run's own handoff files -- step-02-code-designer.json carried a non-schema top-level key `rework_note`, and step-02b-code-design-validator.json carried three non-schema top-level keys (`result_v1_superseded`, `result_v2`, `status_history_note`) left over from its FAIL-then-PASS rework cycle. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's schema has no such keys; a gate step's prior FAIL iteration belongs in `gate_history` (an array of `{iteration, gated_at, status, summary, issues, next_action}` entries), and a producer's own correction note belongs in `result.issues`.

Fixed both files, preserving every fact verbatim, only relocating it into schema-legal fields: step-02's `rework_note` content became a new `result.issues[]` MINOR entry; step-02b's `result_v1_superseded` became `gate_history[0]` (with `gated_at` derived from that FAIL's real commit timestamp, `6f9f689` at 2026-09-17T05:29:20+05:00 = 00:29:20Z, via `git log --follow` on the file), `result_v2` was promoted to the canonical top-level `result`, and `status_history_note` folded into a `result.issues[]` entry. Verified both files still parse as valid JSON and carry only schema-legal top-level keys (python json.load + key-diff against the schema fence). Ran `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` locally and confirmed `0 new violations` (was 2) across the full 2519-file corpus before pushing the fix. (A separate local `mix letflow.check` run in this environment hit Postgres 'too_many_connections' from two concurrent invocations contending for the same local DB pool -- an environment artefact, not evidence of a real code defect, since this fix touches only handoff JSON metadata and no lib/test code; the lint task itself, which was the actual CI failure, was verified directly and separately.)

Committed (`2a96d473`) and pushed the schema fix. Re-polled `gh pr checks 1472` synchronously; this time 'Detect changed paths' (7s), 'Frontend gate (npm run check)' (54s), and 'Backend gate (mix letflow.check)' (9m11s) all passed -- confirmed via the real `gh pr checks` output, no flake exception needed this round.

Confirmed squash-merge is this repo's convention: `gh pr list --state merged --limit 5` plus `git log -1` on PR #1471's merge commit (6ad5ab2c) showed a single commit carrying the PR title with a `(#1471)` suffix -- the signature of a squash merge, not a merge commit or rebase-merge. Ran `gh pr merge 1472 --squash --delete-branch`, which fast-forwarded local main to `958a27b2` and reported the file-level diff landing (docs/issues/ISS-0692.yaml, the five handoffs/WF03-ISS0692-20260917/*.json files, the design doc, and visual-baseline.ts). `git fetch origin main && git log --oneline -3 origin/main` confirms `958a27b2 docs(ISS-0692): REQ-362 visual-baseline design gains binding synthetic-data-only policy (#1472)` is the tip of main.

Independently re-verified the merged content by reading it directly from `origin/main` (not the PR diff view): `git show origin/main:lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md` confirms `### 1.5 Data-sensitivity policy for baseline content (binding, not an open question)` at line 129, the synthetic/disclosed-fictional-data-only invariant text, the redaction/accepted-risk rejection reasoning, both §2.2/§4.1 'Precondition (§1.5)' cross-references, and §7's new AC-map row. `git show origin/main:docs/issues/ISS-0692.yaml` confirms `status: resolved`, `resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0692-20260917`. `git show origin/main:web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts` confirms both JSDoc cross-references to design §1.5 above `acceptBaseline` and `rebaseline`.

This handoff file itself could not be included in PR #1472 (it documents work completed after that PR was already merged), so per the same GIT_MERGE.md constraint the WF03-ISS0699 Step Final precedent (handoffs/WF03-ISS0699-20260917/step-final-git-merge.json) followed, it is landed via a small separate follow-up doc-only PR rather than a direct push to main.

issues.description: CI's backend gate genuinely failed once on this run's own handoff files (non-schema top-level keys: rework_note, result_v1_superseded, result_v2, status_history_note), not on a flake. Root cause: prior WF03-ISS0692-20260917 steps (CODE-DESIGNER's rework, CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's re-gate) invented ad-hoc top-level fields to record a FAIL-and-rework cycle instead of using HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's existing gate_history mechanism. Fixed in commit 2a96d473 on this run's branch (now squashed into 958a27b2 on main). Flagging so future CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR/CODE-DESIGNER rework cycles use gate_history/result.issues from the start rather than inventing a field, avoiding this class of CI-time discovery.
